name: Dominica
summary_text: Dominica demands real caution. High Court decriminalised same-sex relations in April 2024 (fourth Eastern Caribbean state); the old law had allowed forced psychiatric commitment. No LGR; small community; no documented anti-trans violence pattern.

sources.title: Dominica High Court Decriminalizes Same-Sex Conduct | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Apr 2024): 'Dominica High Court Decriminalizes Same-Sex Conduct' — the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court strikes down 'buggery' and 'indecency' provisions as discriminatory.

sources.title: Dominica High Court overturns ban on same-sex relations
sources.claim_summary: BBC (April 2024): Dominica's High Court overturned the ban on consensual same-sex relations - sections 14 and 16 of the Sexual Offences Act were unconstitutional, breaching liberty, expression and privacy rights. The claimant said the laws had condemned him 'to live in constant fear of criminal sanction'; activists hailed 'a significant milestone' for the Caribbean.
NOTE: This is a State Department press statement page (archived, navigation only at fetch time); the underlying statement relates to Dominica.

sources.title: Challenge to Dominica's buggery laws filed in Dominica High Court - Dominica News Online
sources.claim_summary: Dominica News Online (July 2019): a challenge to Dominica's buggery laws was filed in the High Court by a gay man claiming the law violates numerous constitutional rights; represented by Cara Shillingford with support from Minority Rights Dominica (MiRiDom), the Canadian HIV/AIDS Legal Network, University of Toronto's IHRP and Lawyers Without Borders; Maurice Tomlinson announced the case.

sources.title: Catholic bishop in Dominica: End anti-homosexuality laws
sources.claim_summary: Erasing 76 Crimes (May 2013): Dominica's Catholic bishop Gabriel Malzaire called for eliminating criminal penalties for homosexuality and ending 'all forms of violence' against LGBT people, citing the Holy See's UN position; the law provides up to 10 years; notes two men on a gay cruise were arrested in March 2012 for sex on board their ship (released after pleading guilty to indecent exposure).
